minutes.headline: Sewer Commission backed moving billing to the new meter system first and sent its consultant's report questions to Woodard & Curran.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission met remotely and discussed the draft Woodard & Curran I&I report, the business manager's meter import project, and the pump station operations RFP. It voted to keep a commissioner as liaison to send his list of questions to the consultant, and approved the flow assessment contracts and prior minutes. Pump station jetting findings, wipes clogging pumps and failing manhole covers were raised in public comment by the DPW director.

public_comment.topic: A member reported on pump station jetting, wipes clogging pumps, sand infiltration needing camera work, and shoddy manhole covers needing repair.
A commissioner asked that the earlier jetting and manhole comments be placed on a future agenda.

votes.motion: Keep Carl as liaison with the third party, forward his list of questions to Woodard and Curran, and work toward a meeting to discuss answers.
Accept the flow assessment monitoring contract and the equipment leasing contract.

budget_items.what_was_said: Twelve accounts have not paid the annual fee and will get no irrigation credit on the next sewer invoice.
Estimate rose from the earlier figure to a larger number of hours; the town manager is aware and budget hours were allocated.
Quarterly maintenance cost is unchanged from past years; approval to sign was sought.
Lease covers repair and replacement of obsolete equipment, and is in the budget separate from the main flow contract.
The chair asked that pump damage costs from COVID wipes be checked for possible reimbursement.

decisions.decision: Business manager authorized to start converting the billing/meter import project and provide a schedule to the commission, town manager and others.
Draft report review likely pushed to the 25th meeting with the final report targeted for September 11, if the consultant agrees.
One or two members to attend the pre-bid conference; a Zoom link to be sent to members.
New legal counsel policy to be sent next week for approval.
Irrigation meter policy public hearing to be held at the 25th meeting and again later.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to keep a commissioner as liaison with the third party and forward his list of questions on the draft I&I report to Woodard & Curran.
The commission voted to accept the flow assessment monitoring contract and the equipment leasing contract.
The business manager was authorized to start converting the billing meter import project and to give the commission and town manager a schedule.
Review of the draft report is likely to move to the 25th meeting, with a final report targeted for September 11 if the consultant agrees.
The irrigation meter policy public hearing is to be held at the 25th meeting and again later.

why_it_matters: Sewer bills depend on the meter data and billing system now being converted, and the consultant's I&I report will shape what the commission does about groundwater and stormwater entering the sewer.

The irrigation meter policy hearing and the pump station operations bid affect how irrigation credits are given and who runs and maintains the pump stations, and the town budget, mostly taxes, and sewer rates pay for repairs such as wipes damage.
watch_next: Public hearing on the irrigation meter policy at the 25th meeting.
Final Woodard & Curran I&I report, targeted for September 11 if the consultant agrees.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the one clear vote (accepting the flow assessment contracts) and the $5,400 lease, but differ on several items. The main difference is that our minutes record a passed vote on Carl as liaison, and the official minutes show only a suggestion with no vote. They also differ on who attends the pre-bid conference, whether the legal policy goes out for approval or discussion, the project hours, and the attendee list.
